name: Genetic Skin Vascular Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic Skin Vascular Disorder Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of multiple cutaneous vascular malformations including telangiectasias and capillary malformations
Positive family history of similar vascular skin lesions consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutation in known associated gene (e.g., RASA1, EPHB4)
Episodes of recurrent spontaneous bleeding from skin lesions
Lack of significant visceral vascular malformations or systemic involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including cutaneous vascular malformations and positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical evaluation remains primary.

laboratory: Mild anemia on complete blood count due to chronic blood loss
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing superficial cutaneous vascular malformations
MRI angiography to exclude deep or visceral vascular involvement
genetic: Mutations in EPHB4 gene associated with vascular malformations
other: Histopathology of skin biopsy showing dilated capillaries and venules
Family pedigree analysis consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in ENG or ACVRL1 genes
Presence of arteriovenous malformations in multiple organs
Distinct genetic mutations (RASA1) with systemic involvement

redFlags: Sudden onset of extensive bleeding from skin lesions
Neurological deficits suggestive of cerebral vascular malformations
